corn.name: Corn
corn.takes: A heavy feeder. Pulls lots of nitrogen out of the soil.
corn.givesText: Stalks and roots left behind add a little organic matter.

tomato.name: Tomatoes
tomato.takes: A heavy feeder. Needs lots of nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and calcium.
tomato.givesText: Not much for the soil, but tomatoes sell for the most.

potato.name: Potatoes
potato.takes: Uses lots of potassium to grow big tubers.
potato.givesText: Nothing. Digging up the potatoes breaks apart soil crumbs.

beans.name: Beans
beans.takes: Very little. Beans make their own nitrogen.
beans.givesText: Adds nitrogen! Bacteria in little root bumps (nodules) pull nitrogen from the air into the soil.

carrot.name: Carrots
carrot.takes: A light feeder. Needs a little potassium.
carrot.givesText: Long taproots push through packed soil and leave channels for air and water.

wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.givesText: Straw left on the field adds organic matter, and a mat of fine roots holds soil in place.

squash.name: Squash
squash.givesText: Giant leaves shade the ground like a living mulch: fewer weeds and less erosion.

sunflower.name: Sunflowers
sunflower.givesText: Deep taproots break up hard layers and pull up nutrients from deep down. Bees love them.

buckwheat.name: Buckwheat
buckwheat.takes: Very little. Grows well in poor soil.
buckwheat.givesText: Grows so fast it smothers weeds, unlocks phosphorus for the next crop, and adds organic matter.

clover.name: Clover (cover crop)
clover.takes: Almost nothing. It's grown to feed the soil, not to sell.
clover.givesText: A cover crop: roots hold the soil, root nodules add nitrogen, and digging it in (green manure) adds organic matter.
